findings.summary: The plan copies a lock-and-probe mechanism that already exists and is tested in athena-git.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs:161-174: `Snapshot::lock` already removes write bits (`set_tree_writable`), runs `chattr -R +i` on a best-effort basis (`set_immutable`, line 459), probes by creating a file and opening an existing file for write (`probe_write`), and unlocks then fails if a probe succeeds. `unlock_dir` (line 389) is already public. The plan writes a second copy of all this in core and gives as its reason that it 'touches another crate for a one-line shell-out'. In fact about 60 lines would be copied, and the two copies could drift apart. Fix: Move the body of `Snapshot::lock` into a public `athena_git::snapshot::lock_dir(dir)` and have `Snapshot::lock` call it. The evidence snapshot then calls the same function, so there is one lock, one probe and one unlock. The out-of-scope list excludes only the e5sg landing changes in athena-git, not every athena-git change. If athena-git must stay untouched, say in the plan that the core copy has to match `Snapshot::lock` exactly, and test both copies against the same probes.

findings.summary: The parity test could pass by accident, because both views are computed in the same repository.
findings.evidence: The test calls `status_from_snapshot(dir)` and `status()` on the same `Athena`, whose git repository holds the same records. If `status_from_snapshot` mistakenly read `Records::load(&self.git, head)`, throughput would still match. Criterion 3 catches this at the CLI level, but criterion 2 on its own does not show that the data came from the snapshot. Fix: Run `status_from_snapshot` on an `Athena` opened over a second one-commit repository with no `records/`, the same way the criterion 3 fixture is built. Then compare its throughput with `status()` from the fixture repository.

findings.summary: The stored brief is made path-free with a hand-written `replace` instead of the redactor that already exists for this.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:236-249: `Athena::redactor` already maps the state root to `<state>`, the job dir to `<job>` and HOME to `~`, and the redactor is already built in `dispatch` (mod.rs:755). A plain `brief.replace(state_root, "<state>")` misses the HOME form and any non-canonical spelling of the path that the redactor handles. Fix: Produce the stored text with the redactor already in scope in `dispatch` (and `verification.rs`), and hash that text. Keep the criterion 1 assertion that no absolute state path or home path appears in either stored brief.

findings.summary: The brief tells agents to run `athena status --snapshot`, but in a producer's copy the binary is only reachable through `cargo run`, and only when the repository is Athena itself.
findings.evidence: The plan rejects adding `athena` to producer_commands and relies on `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot`. That works only when the job's repository is the Athena workspace. Criterion 4's assertion asks for the sentence 'use `athena status --snapshot <path>`', which a producer cannot run as written. Fix: Have the brief name the command the agent can actually run: Read/Grep on `<path>/records` and `<path>/history.json`, and `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <path>` when working in this repository. Make the criterion 4 assertion check for that text.

summary: I read the code behind each part of the plan, and it matches the snapshot. `dispatch` builds `brief` at run/mod.rs:791. It stores that text verbatim as brief-producer.md (mod.rs:868) and hashes it (mod.rs:857), so the stored brief would contain the real evidence path unless the plan's placeholder step replaces it. `agent_spec` (reading.rs:218-280) builds the hook Policy for every role that goes through it. `confine` (policy.rs:395) denies any path outside `root`, and `Policy` has `deny_unknown_fields`, so a `read_roots` field with a serde default is a sound design. `ClaudeCodeDriver::settings` (claude.rs:151) writes only the hook today. `Records::load` (store.rs:309-384) reads `records/` at the given commit, plus landings from that commit and from the tip of the records branch. The plan copies both. `BOOTSTRAP_OUTCOME` is `records/jobs/bootstrap/outcome.json`, which is inside the copied tree. `status()` (status.rs:1632) loads everything from `self.head()`, so parity holds as long as the same records are read. Every criterion has a seam that exists today: the recording driver in run/tests.rs, the status fixtures, the CLI common harness, and the briefs.rs unit tests. The read-only check runs the root control the defaults require and fails rather than skips. The extra files are explained, and Athena has already flagged them. I found no blocker or major problem. The four minor points: the plan copies a lock mechanism that already exists in athena-git; one test could pass by accident; the stored brief is made safe with a hand-written string replace instead of the existing redactor; and the brief text assumes an `athena` binary is reachable. One residual risk is named honestly: Claude Code may not honour `additionalDirectories`.
